correctness.rationale: For all integers k>=1, exact pilot tails are (9k+1)/16 and 1/16, rank budgets match at ell+3, the specific decision test is strictly true, and the diffuse one/mixed MSE ratio exactly equals (4k+1)(1-1/(192k)). For the concentrated spectrum, as epsilon tends to zero, the one MSE vanishes and mixed MSE tends to a fixed positive number. This proves the two-pilot information lower bound. Three-step Lanczos is exact because the ideal preconditioned matrices have at most three eigenvalues. The delivered standard-library program passed 5575 finite checks; the universal proof is analytic.

General adaptive Hutch++ work uses a different information model. Searches of published records did not identify a covering theorem; novelty remains best-knowledge, not certified worldwide.
residual_risks: An unlocated historical work may contain an equivalent decision-information counterexample.

The best spectral rank projections are oracles under the source ideal cost abstraction.

value.rationale: The precise diagnostic insufficiency is motivated by a recent proposed heuristic and resolves a nontrivial information limitation: two exact Frobenius tail energies cannot identify the spectrum localization needed to compare Gaussian trace MSE across ranks. The unbounded loss is exhibited with well-conditioned regularized matrices and exactly terminated three-step Lanczos, isolating allocation from conditioning and quadrature artifacts. It is not a routine algebraic restatement or a claim about unexamined implementations.
